newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Striking stevedores occupy vessels at Santos port.
newsitem.headline: Striking stevedores occupy vessels at Santos port.

text.p: Striking stevedores at the key Brazilian port of Santos have occupied two vessels docked at the private terminals of steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa), officials said.
"The stevedores boarded a vessel docked at the Cosipe private terminal at dawn, and at midday there was a second invasion of around 40 people," a spokesman for Cosipe said.

"There are two vessels docked at the Cosipe private terminal. Both have been boarded by stevedores and deputies of the Workers' Party, among them Telma de Souza, the former mayor of the city of Santos," the spokesman added.
A spokeswoman at the port authority said Cosipe had asked for reinforcements from the military police.
The stevedores went on strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT over a ruling which allows company workers from Cosipe to conduct loading and unloading at Cosipe's private terminal at the port.
They have been demonstrating in front of Cosipe's facilities since earlier in the day.
The strike is scheduled to last 48 hours and will spread to the national level on Friday, the National Stevedores' Federation said.
Cosipe said a group of 12 stevedores had approached one vessel by sea during the early hours. The second group had entered through the main entrance of Cosipe's factory.
